original_question: If u and v are freely independent unitaries in the ultrapower NU, determine whether they can be lifted to sequences of pairwise k-independent unitaries in N for every k.
target_in_paper: Problem 30 in the section "Lifting problems": the k-independence lifting problem for unitaries in a tracial ultrapower, together with the immediately following note that the freely independent case is already handled in [16]. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the ultrapower setting N^U, that the objects are unitaries, that the issue is a lifting question back to sequences in N, and that the property to be preserved is an independence relation stronger than plain orthogonality. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))
missing_details: The paper's actual open problem is stated for a fixed k-independence level, not as one single statement "for every k" simultaneously. That quantifier should be fixed in advance. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))

The hypothesis in Problem 30 is that the given unitaries are k-independent; your draft instead assumes they are freely independent. The paper explicitly says the freely independent case is already handled in [16], so free independence is too strong if the goal is to match the open problem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))

The standing notation that U is a nonprincipal ultrafilter on N and that N^U denotes the tracial ultrapower of a tracial von Neumann algebra N should be stated explicitly to make the question stand alone. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))
The draft should explicitly place u and v in the unitary group U(N^U), and the lifts in U(N). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))

The meaning of k-independence should be made explicit: the paper recalls it via vanishing trace on alternating centered words, and also says that for unitaries this is equivalently a statement about the von Neumann algebras they generate. Your draft leaves that notion implicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))

For two unitaries, saying the lifts are "pairwise k-independent" is redundant; what is really meant is that at each coordinate n, the pair of lifted unitaries is k-independent in N. The coordinatewise quantifier should be explicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))

The paper also flags Problem 29 as the plain-independence (= 1-independence) version, so if one wants exact paper-faithfulness it helps to note that Problem 30 is the fixed-k generalization of that 1-independent lifting question. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))
refined_question: Fix an integer k >= 1. Let U be a nonprincipal ultrafilter on N, let N be a tracial von Neumann algebra, and write N^U for its tracial ultrapower. If u,v are unitaries in U(N^U) that are k-independent in the paper's sense (equivalently, the abelian von Neumann algebras W*(u) and W*(v) are k-independent, i.e. the trace vanishes on the relevant alternating centered words up to order k), must there exist lifts u = (u_n)_U and v = (v_n)_U with each u_n,v_n in U(N) such that for every n, the pair u_n,v_n is k-independent in N?
justification: The nearest official target is Problem 30, not a broader reformulation: the section "Lifting problems" first recalls the paper's notion of k-independence and then asks whether k-independent unitaries in an ultrapower can be lifted to sequences of coordinatewise k-independent unitaries. The sentence immediately after Problem 30 says that the freely independent case is already handled in [16], which shows that your draft has fused the open problem with its solved special case. The refined version therefore fixes k, restores the standing ultrapower notation, and asks exactly for coordinatewise preservation of k-independence under lifting. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))

citations.label: [16] Cyril Houdayer and Adrian Ioana, "Asymptotic freeness in tracial ultraproducts"
